findings.evidence: The existing text differentiated useful work and cohorts but did not explicitly connect an asynchronous acceptance endpoint to its worker/effect evidence. RFC 9110 distinguishes 202 acceptance from completed processing; k6 expected-response metrics classify the HTTP response, not a downstream business effect.
findings.consequence: A valid open-arrival experiment can show fast green HTTP responses while the claimed business completion objective is missed; adding naive polling can also inflate request counts and VU occupancy.
findings.correction: Trace the real acknowledgement/persistence/worker/effect path; join logical IDs and retain unresolved outcomes; distinguish effect commit from observed visibility; separate submission/status/completion metrics and bound observation load. Preserve admission-only claims and reuse independent completion telemetry.

expectedBehavior: Read the implementation boundary and logical-ID cohort audit rather than infer business success from 202 or zero HTTP failures.
Correct report.md: 4800/6000 reach the required effect in time, below 99%; retain the 1200 unresolved jobs in the denominator.
Explain that all deadlines have passed by the declared follow-up, while unresolved jobs may still complete later and are not demonstrated lost.

failureConditions: Keep a pass verdict based only on HTTP thresholds or job IDs.

Require a fresh load test, new dependency, full profiler capture or a changed arrival model before correcting the report.
Return only advice/questions without updating the artifact.

failureConditions: Repeat the business-effect rejection despite the declared admission boundary.
